paragraphs.text: At No. 5 Middle School, students in Grade One run for twenty minutes every morning before the first class. The school started the activity three years ago, and many students say it has changed their school life.

'I often felt sleepy in class before,' says Wang Bo, a Grade One student. 'Now running wakes my body up, and I can listen to the teachers better.' Doctors agree that morning exercise improves blood flow to the brain and helps young people sleep at night. However, they also warn that students should not run too fast at the beginning, or their knees may get hurt. Warming up for five minutes and drinking some water after the run are simple but useful rules. The school plans to add a health record for each student to show how daily exercise works.
